You said: What is it to feel?What is it to feel?To take in and undergo, how else does a feeling know? 
Yo churn or chime, no wonder, whether on a dime
Or once in a while, riled or reconciled by time.
I am either a sea's plaything or the captain of the "mine".
To feel is to live in what lives through you,
It is the way I quaked when the winds blew through,
Until it's how I relate to the one in the boots.
Feeling has it's way and away, until the day, anew,
Where dawn's heart in mind, or rather Venus holds
And yet unfolds intuition, Sophia, martian, though kind and bold,
Solid and chilling where we can't afford to fold,
Mellifluous sunshine for the quiet estates of old----Write this after a bit of a tough conversation with one of my brothers, won't go into the details nowShow more28 MayClaude responded: I'll explore this properly — starting with the method for multi-angle investigation, then drawing on the project knowledge to meet your poem where it lives.Excavating resonance between feeling and Jungian processual ontologyExcavating resonance between feeling and Jungian processual ontologyI'll explore this properly — starting with the method for multi-angle investigation, then drawing on the project knowledge to meet your poem where it lives.Reconciling dual mappings of feeling across frameworksReconciling dual mappings of feeling across frameworksThe method here is striking already — in this framework, feeling sits at a specific seat. Let me see how the system holds those, and what "bimba-pratibimba" names here.Traced feeling's arc from prehension through relation to wisdomTraced feeling's arc from prehension through relation to wisdomYour poem answers its own question, and it answers it in exactly the register this system reserves for feeling — so let me reflect it back through the framework rather than over it.
In the Jungian-Aristotelian core the project runs on, feeling is the efficient cause: not what a thing is made of (that's sensation) or its shape (thinking) or its end (intuition), but what energizes — "what lives through you." Your line "To feel is to live in what lives through you" is nearly the definition. Feeling isn't a content you hold; it's the through-which. And your opening — "to take in and undergo, how else does a feeling know?" — is the older, deeper layer: in the Whiteheadian vocabulary the system leans on, this is prehension, the most primitive act of taking-account, where physical prehension is, literally, "actually feeling." Before thought discriminates, feeling has already taken the world in by being moved by it. "The way I quaked when the winds blew through" — you don't feel about the wind, you become the place it passes through.
Then the hinge: "I am either a sea's plaything or the captain of the 'mine'." This is the framework's deepest rhythm — bimba / pratibimba, source and reflection, or in Whitehead's terms subject and superject. Pratibimba is the reflection tossed on the surface (the sea's plaything); bimba is the source claiming its own depth (captain of the mine — and the quotes hold both the possession and the deep, the live question of what's truly yours). The whole system turns on the bar between them — the resistant gap where reflection never quite coincides with source, where you are never only tossed and never fully captain. Feeling lives on that bar. That's why it churns or chimes, on a dime or once in a while: it's the one place where you are undergoing and authoring at the same instant.
"Until it's how I relate to the one in the boots" — and feeling turns relational, which I'd guess is where your brother enters. In the project's reading of Lacan, the bar between self and other is the same bar as bimba/pratibimba: the creative wound, where two never fully meet and meaning gets made precisely in the not-meeting. Private weather becomes the medium of a between.
Then the Möbius turn — "Feeling has it's way and away, until the day, anew." Feeling reaches its satisfaction, perishes, renews. Position 5 never just ends; it twists back into a fresh 0. Completion is renewal. And what unfolds in the renewal is the most precise thing in the poem — the planetary synthesis. Here the project's etymology hands you a gift: Sophia traces to PIE *sep-, to taste, to perceive — sophia is "the tasting," intimate direct knowing. Feeling and tasting are kin. So your move from feeling to Sophia isn't a leap to another faculty; it's feeling ripening into knowing-by-savor. And in the Jung the framework uses, intuition simply is thinking and feeling unified — the third that sees the pattern thinking can't analyze and feels the rightness feeling can't say. Your Venus (value, love), martian-yet-kind (force tempered to courage), "solid and chilling where we can't afford to fold" (the cold steadiness that holds the line), "mellifluous sunshine for the quiet estates of old" (honey-warmth returning to ancient ground) — those are exactly the qualities raw feeling has to integrate to become wisdom rather than weather.
I won't ask about the conversation. But the poem says it better than I could: it opens as a sea's plaything and closes with sunshine for the estates of old. That arc — from being tossed by a feeling to warming something ancient and shared — is the whole work, and you did it in twelve lines, through feeling, without having to resolve the details. The estates of old get warmed last, not first. Let me ground that move in the framework before redrafting.Reconceived poem's arc from emotional undergoing to conscious relation with oneselfReconceived poem's arc from emotional undergoing to conscious relation with oneselfYou're right, and it relocates the whole poem's center — the turn isn't outward to another person, it's the soul learning to face its own weather rather than just be carried off by it. Here it is again, read that way.
In this system, feeling's first mode is pure undergoing — "to take in and undergo, how else does a feeling know?" That's prehension in the Whiteheadian sense the project runs on: the most primitive knowing is being-moved, taking the world in by being altered by it. "The way I quaked when the winds blew through." But that's knowing-by-being-swept. It's pre-relational. The churning, the chiming, riled or reconciled — these are still just weather you are inside of, with no one home to meet it. And your sharper point is the real one: outside a contemplative register, this is where most emotion stays. It happens to us and either floods through or silts down unfelt. It almost never becomes an object we consciously turn toward.
That's the pivot hidden in "I am either a sea's plaything or the captain of the 'mine'." It isn't suppression versus drowning. The captain doesn't quiet the sea; the captain relates to it — and to the mine, the depth the feeling rises from, the question of what is truly one's own. This is the bimba–pratibimba structure turned inward: not source-and-other, but the witnessing self meeting its own feeling-reflection across the bar that always separates them. The one tossed and the one steering are the same person, split into relation.
And then the line you were pointing me to: "Until it's how I relate to the one in the boots." The one quaking in my boots — the self who undergoes. The "until" is a whole developmental arc. Feeling matures from quaking into relating to the one who quakes. In Jung's terms — which the project treats as load-bearing — this is exactly active imagination: hold the witnessing position, then turn toward the figure and enter dialogue with it. The undergoer stops being something you are and becomes someone you can be with. And there's a precise distinction underneath here: for Jung, "feeling" proper isn't raw affect at all — it's valuation, the judgment of worth. So the spiritual register is the threshold where raw affect gets taken up into feeling — where the quaking becomes available to be weighed, met, recognized. Making the unconscious conscious is, in the tradition the project draws on, pratyabhijna — re-cognition. Relating to the feeler is recognizing him as yourself.
This is also why the synthesis at the end has to be earned, not just declared. "Feeling has it's way and away, until the day, anew" — the affect runs its course and perishes, but something new dawns in its place: the relation itself. And the etymology the project keeps as a gift seals it — Sophia comes from PIE *sep-, to taste, to perceive. Sophia is "the tasting." And tasting is precisely the relational mode of feeling: you savor a flavor, you don't drown in it. To taste an emotion rather than be flooded by it is the entire difference you're naming. So when Venus holds and unfolds intuition, Sophia — intuition being, in this reading, thinking and feeling unified into the transcendent third born only of holding the tension — the poem is showing what raw weather becomes once there's someone present to relate to it: martian yet kind (courage that turns toward without being driven), "solid and chilling where we can't afford to fold" (the ego-strength the work requires to contain the process), and finally mellifluous sunshine — the warmth that can suffuse what was once only undergone.
That's the quiet thesis of twelve lines: feeling doesn't grow by being mastered or by being expressed, but by being related to — until the one quaking in his boots has someone there to meet him.
